rv.q: Trap Door delivers a substantial piece of theater that is at once pungent social commentary and delightful entertainment.
Burgundia feels like a very familiar kingdom in Jenny Beacraft’s staging.
In this regard, “Princess Ivona” is successful.
But more often than not, you wish more of the cast members were better-honed with their comic timing to earn more slapstick laughs.
Laura Nelson gives a star performance, not exaggerated or self-pitying, but simply allowing Ivona to have naturalistic reactions to the ridiculous people surrounding her.

cn.t: Critics praise this absurdist satire for its daring social commentary and darkly comic exploration of power dynamics, with Trap Door Theatre's intimate production transforming Gombrowicz's proto-absurdist classic into an exhilarating theatrical experience.
